title: Kept Amount of a Returned Property Tax Refund — Reserve Analysis Method
content:
For a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts, the kept amount of a returned property tax refund is the figure defined below. All figures are taken from the reserve's own records on the handling date.

## Definitions

1. **The tax year's bills** are the property tax bills on file for the reserve received within the twelve months before the handling date: received no later than the handling date and fewer than twelve whole calendar months before it.
2. **The overpayment.** Where at least one of the tax year's bills is withdrawn and at least one is received and unpaid (request status received), the refund restores an overpayment equal to the billed amounts of the tax year's paid bills, less the billed amount of the most recently received unpaid property tax bill times the number of those paid bills, never below zero — because the corrected installments of a tax year, 2 to a tax year, are equal. Otherwise there is no overpayment to restore. The most recently received unpaid property tax bill is the reserve's property tax bill with status received and the latest received date.
3. **The horizon.** The reserve period left is the plan's reserve months (the months of property charges the plan funds at closing, shown in the plan matrix) less the whole calendar months from the reserve's established date to the handling date, never below zero; the horizon of the refund review is that many whole months. A month counts as whole only once the handling date reaches the established date's day number.
4. **The tax part** of the reserve's need is the annual property tax on file times the horizon months, divided by twelve.
5. **The insurance part** is the annual hazard premium plus the annual flood premium on file, together times the horizon months, divided by twelve.
6. **The reserve's need** is the tax part plus the insurance part plus the cushion, and the cushion is zero.
7. **The room** is the need less the reserve balance, never below zero.
8. **The excess** is the overpayment less the room, never below zero.
9. **Release.** An excess above zero that is at least the release floor of 50.00 is released to the borrower; a smaller excess stays in the reserve. The borrower keeps the whole released excess.
10. **The kept amount** is the overpayment less the part of the released excess the borrower keeps, rounded half up to the cent once, at the end; no intermediate figure is rounded.

## Worked figures on hypothetical inputs

Tax year's bills: two paid at 1,800.00, one withdrawn at 1,800.00, one received corrected bill at 1,500.00. Overpayment: 3,600.00 less 1,500.00 times 2, which is 600.00. Annual charges on file: tax 3,000.00, hazard 1,200.00, flood 600.00. Suppose the reserve period left is 6 months.

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Tax part: 3,000.00 times 6, divided by 12 | 1,500.00 |
| Insurance part: 1,800.00 times 6, divided by 12 | 900.00 |
| Need (cushion zero) | 2,400.00 |

| Reserve balance | Room | Excess | Released | Kept amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,100.00 | 300.00 | 300.00 | 300.00 | 300.00 |
| 1,840.00 | 560.00 | 40.00 | none (below 50.00) | 600.00 |
| 3,000.00 | 0.00 | 600.00 | 600.00 | 0.00 |
